research_question: Can one declarative public/private-field schema generate observation-invariance obligations that exactly reproduce the independent one-die reference and transfer unchanged to a hidden Goofspiel commitment fault?

scope.mechanism: GameSpec observation field slice plus generic pair generator

one_die_reference_gate.required_equivalence: Every generated ordered state pair must equal the corresponding independently retained manual reference pair.

goofspiel_transfer_gate.semantics: Player 0 commits a currently available card before player 1 acts; that pending card remains private until both submissions are revealed.
goofspiel_transfer_gate.state_coverage: All combinatorially reachable public inventory shapes with two to four cards remaining and every legal current prize and player-0 pending card.

primary_pass_condition: The one-die generated state-pair sequence exactly matches all 5220 manual reference pairs.
The correct one-die and Goofspiel adapters have zero generated-contract violations.
The one-die leak has 5220 information-set-only violations.
The Goofspiel pending-card leak has 1032 information-set-only violations.
The structurally valid Goofspiel leak remains a negative control for structure-only auditing.
interpretation_boundary: Success demonstrates reuse of a declarative observation-contract mechanism across two distinct private-information leaks. It does not prove that the declarations are correct when authored by an LLM, certify full Goofspiel play, or justify adaptive learning from runtime histories.
